name: React Spring
role: Physics-based spring animation for React; velocity-aware, not time-seekable
summary: Spring-physics animation library for React (and other targets) built on useSpring, useTransition and useTrail. Values settle by simulated physics rather than fixed durations, giving natural interruption and velocity carry-over. Because springs are stateful and clocked by requestAnimationFrame, frame-exact seeking needs the frameLoop override or offline sampling, which is unproven here.
use_when: React UI where interruptible, velocity-carrying springs are the point
Over Motion when you want hook-first physics and transitions on lists
Sampling spring curves offline to bake into keyframes
avoid_when: Exact-time seek for capture: GSAP timelines
Sequenced multi-step choreography: GSAP or Motion
Non-React DOM or SVG animation: Anime.js or GSAP
notes: 2026-10-26: offline sampling and a manual frame loop are unverified; the PRD item to evaluate it remains open.

assessment.rationale: Active: v10.1.2 released 2026-06-24, MIT. Well maintained, but spring clock is not externally seekable; keep as catalogued React option behind Motion and GSAP.

evidence.result: 90 frames at 1280x720, shuffled order matches sequential, distinct hashes, frame 45 alpha 0..1, no page errors; react 19.3.1, esbuild 0.25.12, Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4.
evidence.scope: animated.div set via SpringValue.set in flushSync from closed-form t; no spring started or seeked, harness-driven frames; macOS arm64, repo-only; spring physics unproven.
